one_line_contribution: A token-matched factorial inside a live ALFWorld instance that separates the number of world-state changes an agent must carry from the raw token length of its history, plus a head-to-head of seven context managers scored by which of those two loads each one actually removes.
closest_prior_work: WMF-AM (arXiv:2603.27343, verified via s2cli: 'Probing LLM Working Memory via Depth-Parameterized Cumulative State Tracking', 2026-03-28, 4 citations) is the biggest threat, because it is the same claim one step earlier: cumulative state tracking across K sequential updates is the load that matters, K is already the manipulated variable, 28 models are already covered, and it already ships a ReAct battery correlation (tau 0.595) plus a load-shift pilot. This proposal's diagnostic half is essentially that pilot de-confounded and moved into an environment — a real methodological upgrade, but a derivative one, and a reviewer will ask why this is a paper rather than a rebuttal appendix to WMF-AM. Second threat, and one the proposal never cites: SABER (arXiv:2512.07850, verified via s2cli, 2025-11-26, 14 citations, 'Small Actions, Big Errors: Safeguarding Mutating Steps in LLM Agents'), whose headline analysis is that mutating (state-changing) actions, not sheer trajectory growth, account for most long-horizon agent errors, and which also ships block-based context cleaning as a fix. SABER argues at the action level and does not run a token-matched length control, so it does not scoop the factorial — but it does scoop the punchline, and it means P1's positive arm confirms a published finding. Third: the 2026 state-tracking cluster I verified (LongHorizon-Harness 2608.01964, StateM 2608.15089, LongDS-Bench 2605.30434, WorldLines 2606.18847, Long-Horizon Task Mirage 2604.11978) has already made 'state, not length' the field's working assumption, which is why the interesting result here is the LENGTH null, not the STATE effect — and the LENGTH null is exactly the arm that is underpowered by construction (see strongest_objection).
strongest_objection: The central contrast is confounded on entity mentions, and the length arm is a strawman. (a) STATE-IRRELEVANT and LENGTH differ in far more than state-changingness: a relocation prefix names objects and receptacles and produces diverse, entity-rich observations; a prefix padded with examine/look/inventory produces repetitive low-entropy text mentioning far fewer distinct entities. So the predicted gradient LENGTH < STATE-IRRELEVANT < DISTRACTOR is equally well read as a single monotone entity-interference function, with 'semantic similarity to the target' as the only thing that changes across arms. DISTRACTOR does not rescue this, because DISTRACTOR is defined by similarity to the target while STATE-IRRELEVANT still floods the context with real in-scene entities; P3's concavity contrast distinguishes two shapes of the same interference curve, not two causes. P2 — the load of the proposal, since it is the arm that says failure is not retrieval — is uninterpretable without an entity-matched control. (b) K in {4,8,16} ALFWorld actions is roughly 0.2-1.5K tokens of prefix. arXiv:2510.05381 (verified: EMNLP, 150 citations) demonstrated the length-alone effect over tens of thousands of tokens. Declaring in the abstract that 'the length-alone effect is below the noise floor at the lengths agents actually reach' from a contrast that never leaves the kilotoken regime is not a test of that paper, it is a range restriction; P6's 'LENGTH remains null at every scale' is guaranteed by the design, not discovered by it, and an area chair will read the headline as overclaimed. (c) A smaller but real hit: P4's mediation ('conditional success given the relocation is mentioned is indistinguishable from full context') conditions on a post-treatment mediator that is not randomly assigned — summaries that happen to capture the relocation come from episodes that are plausibly easier on other dimensions, so the conditional comparison is a collider, not a mechanism test. (d) The deterministic scratchpad is a ground-truth state oracle parsed from ALFWorld's regular grammar; P4's 'it closes 70% of the gap at 30% of the tokens' is close to true by construction, and the proposal's own limitations section concedes it is an upper bound, which leaves the portable arm (LLM-maintained scratchpad) carrying the entire generalizable claim.
what_would_fix_it: Four changes, in order of how much they buy. (1) Add the entity-matched non-state-changing arm described in missing_baseline, and pre-register that P2 counts only if STATE-IRRELEVANT beats that arm, not merely LENGTH; this converts the study from 'state vs length' (already believed) to 'state change vs mere entity mention' (genuinely open, and the result could go either way). (2) Decouple state count from token budget as fully crossed factors rather than matching within K: run K in {4,8,16} at padded total prefix budgets of roughly 1K/8K/32K real non-state-changing tokens, so the length axis actually spans the regime where 2510.05381 measured its effect and the interaction K x tokens becomes estimable. Without this the paper cannot say anything about the length account at all. (3) Randomize the mediator in P4: inject an oracle relocation line into a random subset of LLM summaries and compare against summaries where it is absent by chance, turning the omission story into an experiment. (4) Report expected base rates: 'at least 8 points at K=16 on the 8B backbone' is the load-bearing prediction, and 8B ReAct on ALFWorld frequently sits low enough that a floor effect eats the contrast and breaks the assumed 0.2 discordance behind the MDE. Also fix the citation of arXiv:2607.03441, which I verified as 'No Time Like the Present: Agentic Test-Time Training' — a token-reweighting training method, not a report of repeated-n-gram-induced in-context drift on ALFWorld. Separately, the compute must be cut to survive the stated budget: the diagnostic phase alone is 800 x 5 x 3 = 12k episodes per backbone, the manager phase multiplies that by seven managers, and with three backbones plus ScienceWorld plus eight ablations plus WMF-AM this is well into six figures of ReAct episodes on 4xA100 with a 120B MoE served locally. Drop to one backbone x full factorial, two backbones x a reduced grid, and move ScienceWorld to a single confirmatory cell.
missing_baseline: An ENTITY-MATCHED non-state-changing prefix: examine/look actions issued over exactly the objects and receptacles that the relocation prefix touches, producing observations that name the same entities in the same quantity, but leaving the world unchanged. This is the only arm that separates 'the world changed and the agent must carry it' from 'many distinct in-scene entities were mentioned', and its absence makes P2 — the proposal's load-bearing prediction — attributable to entity interference rather than state load. The listed 'alternate LENGTH prefix using varied non-state actions' is offered as a robustness check against repetition and is explicitly not matched on entity count, so it does not fill the hole. A second, cheaper omission worth adding: a NARRATED-RELOCATION arm in which the prefix text describes K relocations that were never enacted, which separates the cost of tracking a described state change from the cost of the world actually being different.

All eight of my queries were answered by channel (a), the s2cli command (s2 + HF sub-channels both returned ok on every call); WebSearch was unavailable in this session and WebFetch is blocked, so channel (b) answered nothing. IDs I verified with s2cli paper or direct search hits: 2603.27343 (WMF-AM, framing matches the proposal's description), 2608.01964 (LongHorizon-Harness), 2510.00615 (ACON), 2510.12635 (Memory-as-Action), 2510.05381, 2605.10828, 2607.08716, 2512.07850, 2604.11978, 2604.17091, 2605.24941, 2607.03441 (verified to exist but its content is agentic test-time training, NOT the ALFWorld repeated-n-gram drift result the proposal attributes to it). IDs I could NOT verify in this session: 2605.05191 (LongSeeker), 2603.04257 (Memex), 2602.12108 (StateLM), 2601.04463 (ProMem), 2608.12990, 2608.04530, 2605.12233, 2601.08079. Judging the proposal's own check: it is above average for naming channels, queries and IDs, but it self-reports that two of its intended WebSearch queries — both on the length-alone claim it is trying to overturn — 'were issued but not executed (session search budget exhausted)', and it verified its single most load-bearing citation (WMF-AM) through WebFetch, a channel the reviewer cannot audit and the rules forbid. It also missed SABER (2512.07850, 2025-11-26, 14 citations), which already publishes the claim that state-mutating actions rather than context growth drive long-horizon agent errors, and missed the 2026 harness cluster (2608.15089, 2608.01964, 2605.30434, 2606.18847) that treats state tracking as the settled diagnosis. None of these runs the token-matched factorial, so novelty on the design survives; what does not survive is the framing that 'state, not length' is an open question.
